> **Note:** This is pilot data. Any statistical tests are included as a structural scaffold for when the full sample is collected — interpret results cautiously with small N.

## 1. Packages & data

```{r packages}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(knitr)
library(lmerTest)    # mixed models with Satterthwaite p-values
library(emmeans)     # post-hoc pairwise comparisons
library(patchwork)   # combine ggplots
```

```{r config}
find_project_root <- function() {
  start <- dirname(rstudioapi::getSourceEditorContext()$path)
  current <- normalizePath(start, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)
  
  repeat {
    config_path <- file.path(current, "config.R")
    
    if (file.exists(config_path)) {
      return(current)
    }
    
    parent <- dirname(current)
    
    if (parent == current) {
      stop("Could not find config.R in this directory or any parent directory.")
    }
    
    current <- parent
  }
}

project_dir <- find_project_root()
config_path <- file.path(project_dir, "config.R")

source(config_path)
clean_data_dir <- COMBINED_PSYCHO_DIR

# ── Participant selection ── edit analysis/participant_status.csv, not this chunk.
# Main-study participants only by default; set TRUE to also analyse the pilots.
INCLUDE_PILOTS <- FALSE
analysis_dir <- if (basename(project_dir) == "analysis") project_dir else file.path(project_dir, "analysis")
PARTICIPANT_STATUS_PATH <- file.path(analysis_dir, "participant_status.csv")
source(file.path(analysis_dir, "participant_status.R"), local = TRUE)
```

```{r load}
cond_levels <- c("baseline", "negative_induction", "post_negative_induction_recovery",
                 "positive_induction", "post_positive_induction_recovery")

d <- read_csv(file.path(clean_data_dir, "biosignals2_selfreport_ratings.csv"),
              show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(condition = factor(condition, levels = cond_levels))

# Main-study participants only (plus pilots if INCLUDE_PILOTS) — see participant_status.csv
dropped <- participants_dropped(d$participant_id, INCLUDE_PILOTS)
d <- d |> filter(participant_keep(participant_id, INCLUDE_PILOTS))

n_participants <- n_distinct(d$participant_id)
cat("Participants:", n_participants, "\n")
cat("Rows        :", nrow(d), "\n")
```

```{r participants-left-out}
# Who participant_status.csv left out of this analysis
if (nrow(dropped)) knitr::kable(dropped, caption = paste0(
  "Left out of this analysis (", nrow(dropped), "); edit participant_status.csv to change. ",
  "Pilots ", if (INCLUDE_PILOTS) "included" else "excluded", " (INCLUDE_PILOTS = ", INCLUDE_PILOTS, ")"
)) else cat("No participants left out.\n")
```

```{r theme}
theme_set(
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +

        strip.background  = element_rect(fill = "grey92"),

)

# Condition colours (five-level palette)
cond_colours <- c(
  baseline                          = "#5B8DB8",
  negative_induction                = "#E07B54",
  post_negative_induction_recovery  = "#F2C4B0",
```

## 2. Data quality checks

### 2.1 Observations per participant and condition

```{r obs-count}
d |>
  count(participant_id, condition) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = condition, values_from = n) |>
  kable(caption = "Number of rows per participant × condition")
```

### 2.2 Missing values in key columns

```{r missing}
d |>
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.)))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "column", values_to = "n_missing") |>
  filter(n_missing > 0) |>
  arrange(desc(n_missing)) |>
  kable(caption = "Columns with missing values")
```

### 2.3 Rating range check

All slider responses should be integers between 1 and 7.

```{r range-check}
response_cols <- names(d)[str_detect(names(d), "_valence$|_arousal$|_approach$|_intensity$") &
                          !str_detect(names(d), "_rt$|_order$")]

d |>
  select(all_of(response_cols)) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "scale", values_to = "value") |>
  drop_na(value) |>
  group_by(scale) |>
  summarise(
    n    = n(),
    min  = min(value),
    max  = max(value),
    any_out_of_range = any(value < 1 | value > 7),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  kable(caption = "Rating range check (expected: 1–7)")
```

### 2.4 Reaction time distributions

RTs below \~0.5 s on a deliberate slider task are suspicious (likely accidental clicks). Flag and inspect any such responses.

```{r rt-check}
rt_cols <- names(d)[str_detect(names(d), "_rt$")]

rt_long <- d |>
  select(participant_id, condition, all_of(rt_cols)) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(participant_id, condition), names_to = "scale", values_to = "rt") |>
  drop_na(rt)

rt_long |>
  filter(rt < 0.5) |>
  kable(caption = "Responses with RT < 0.5 s (flag for review)")
```

```{r rt-plot, fig.height=5}
rt_long |>
  mutate(scale = str_remove(scale, "_rt$")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = rt, y = fct_reorder(scale, rt, median, .na_rm = TRUE),
             colour = participant_id)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7, size = 2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", colour = "red", linewidth = 0.5) +
  labs(title = "Reaction time per scale", x = "RT (s)", y = NULL,
       colour = "Participant") +
  theme(legend.position = "right")
```

### 2.5 Trigger name check

Confirm every video row has a trigger name (needed to link to physiology).

```{r trigger-check}
d |>
  select(participant_id, video_id, trigger_name) |>
  mutate(trigger_missing = is.na(trigger_name)) |>
  kable(caption = "Trigger names — NA indicates a failed lookup")
```

## 3. Descriptive statistics

### 3.1 Summary table

```{r summary-table}
rating_cols <- c("stim_valence", "stim_arousal", "stim_approach",
                 "stim_emotion_intensity",
                 "block_start_valence", "block_start_arousal",
                 "block_end_valence",   "block_end_arousal")

d |>
  select(participant_id, condition, all_of(rating_cols)) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(participant_id, condition),
               names_to = "measure", values_to = "value") |>
  drop_na(value) |>
  group_by(condition, measure) |>
  summarise(
    n    = n(),
    mean = round(mean(value), 2),
    sd   = round(sd(value),   2),
    min  = min(value),
    max  = max(value),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(measure, condition) |>
  kable(caption = "Descriptive statistics by condition and measure")
```

### 3.2 Stimulus ratings by condition and video

```{r stim-ratings-plot}
d |>
  filter(condition %in% c("negative_induction", "positive_induction")) |>
  select(participant_id, condition, video_id,
         stim_valence, stim_arousal, stim_approach) |>
  pivot_longer(starts_with("stim_"),
               names_to = "measure", values_to = "value",
               names_prefix = "stim_") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = condition, y = value, colour = condition)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.1, height = 0, size = 3, seed = 42) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "crossbar",
               width = 0.4, linewidth = 0.7, colour = "black") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = cond_colours, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(1, 7), breaks = 1:7) +
  facet_wrap(~measure, ncol = 3) +
  labs(title = "Stimulus ratings by condition",
       subtitle = "Points = individual videos; crossbar = mean",
       x = NULL, y = "Rating (1–7)")
```

```{r stim-ratings-per-video, fig.height=6}
d |>
  filter(condition %in% c("negative_induction", "positive_induction")) |>
  select(participant_id, condition, video_id,
         stim_valence, stim_arousal, stim_approach) |>
  pivot_longer(c(stim_valence, stim_arousal, stim_approach),
               names_to = "measure", values_to = "value",
               names_prefix = "stim_") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = video_id, y = value, fill = condition)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.5, outlier.shape = NA, width = 0.6) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.8,
             position = position_jitter(width = 0.1, seed = 42)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cond_colours) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(1, 7), breaks = 1:7) +
  facet_wrap(~ measure, ncol = 1) +
  labs(title = "Stimulus ratings per video",
       subtitle = "Points = individual participant ratings",
       x = NULL, y = "Rating (1–7)", fill = "Condition") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
```

```{r stim-ratings-table}
d |>
  filter(condition %in% c("negative_induction", "positive_induction")) |>
  group_by(condition, video_id) |>
  summarise(
    n              = n(),
    mean_valence   = round(mean(stim_valence,  na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    mean_arousal   = round(mean(stim_arousal,  na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    mean_approach  = round(mean(stim_approach, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(condition, video_id) |>
  kable(caption = "Mean stimulus ratings per video")
```

### 3.3 State rating trajectories

State valence and arousal across the four rating timepoints. Pre- and post-baseline are shared starting points; the negative and positive arms then diverge.

`block_start_valence`/`block_start_arousal` = state before the baseline fixation cross (pre-baseline rating, only collected once per session and stored on the `baseline` row). `block_end_valence`/`block_end_arousal` = state at the end of each block.

```{r trajectory-data}
# Six-point trajectory reflecting the fixed condition order:
# pre-baseline → post-baseline → negative induction →
# negative recovery → positive induction → positive recovery.

trajectory_levels <- c("Pre-baseline", "Post-baseline",
                        "Negative induction", "Negative recovery",
                        "Positive induction", "Positive recovery")

trajectory <- bind_rows(
  d |> filter(condition == "baseline") |>
    distinct(participant_id, valence = block_start_valence, arousal = block_start_arousal) |>
    mutate(timepoint = "Pre-baseline"),
  d |> filter(condition == "baseline") |>
    distinct(participant_id, valence = block_end_valence, arousal = block_end_arousal) |>
    mutate(timepoint = "Post-baseline"),
  d |> filter(condition == "negative_induction") |>
    distinct(participant_id, valence = block_end_valence, arousal = block_end_arousal) |>
    mutate(timepoint = "Negative induction"),
  d |> filter(condition == "post_negative_induction_recovery") |>
    distinct(participant_id, valence = block_end_valence, arousal = block_end_arousal) |>
    mutate(timepoint = "Negative recovery"),
  d |> filter(condition == "positive_induction") |>
    distinct(participant_id, valence = block_end_valence, arousal = block_end_arousal) |>
    mutate(timepoint = "Positive induction"),
  d |> filter(condition == "post_positive_induction_recovery") |>
    distinct(participant_id, valence = block_end_valence, arousal = block_end_arousal) |>
    mutate(timepoint = "Positive recovery")
) |>
  mutate(timepoint = factor(timepoint, levels = trajectory_levels))
```

```{r trajectory-plot}
trajectory |>
  pivot_longer(c(valence, arousal), names_to = "measure", values_to = "value") |>
  drop_na(value) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = timepoint, y = value,
             group = participant_id, colour = participant_id)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(1, 7), breaks = 1:7) +
  scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(angle = 30)) +
  facet_wrap(~measure, ncol = 2) +
  labs(title  = "State ratings across timepoints",
       x = NULL, y = "Rating (1–7)", colour = "Participant")
```

## 4. Condition effects

One-way repeated measures ANOVA with `condition` as the within-subjects factor, run separately for `block_end_valence` and `block_end_arousal`. Models are fit with `lmer` (random intercept per participant), with the omnibus test via `anova()` and Bonferroni-corrected pairwise comparisons via `emmeans`.

```{r manip-check-compute}
# Manipulation check: change in state valence/arousal from post-baseline to post-induction.
# block_end_valence of "baseline" condition = post-baseline rating.
# block_end_valence of induction conditions = post-induction rating.

baseline_end <- d |>
  filter(condition == "baseline") |>
  distinct(participant_id,
           baseline_valence = block_end_valence,
           baseline_arousal = block_end_arousal)

manip_check <- d |>
  filter(condition %in% c("negative_induction", "positive_induction")) |>
  distinct(participant_id, condition, block_end_valence, block_end_arousal) |>
  left_join(baseline_end, by = "participant_id") |>
  mutate(
    manip_check_valence = block_end_valence - baseline_valence,
    manip_check_arousal = block_end_arousal - baseline_arousal,
    manip_check_direction_correct = case_when(
      condition == "positive_induction" & manip_check_valence > 0 ~ TRUE,
      condition == "negative_induction" & manip_check_valence < 0 ~ TRUE,
      is.na(manip_check_valence)                                  ~ NA,
      TRUE                                                        ~ FALSE
    )
  )
```

```{r model-data}
# One row per participant × condition for block-end state ratings.
# distinct() is needed because induction conditions repeat block_end across video rows.
block_end_ratings <- d |>
  distinct(participant_id, condition, block_end_valence, block_end_arousal) |>
  drop_na(block_end_valence)
```

### 4.1 Manipulation check

Did the emotion induction shift state valence in the expected direction?

```{r manip-check-plot}
manip_check |>
  ggplot(aes(x = condition, y = manip_check_valence, colour = condition,
             group = participant_id)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_line(colour = "grey60") +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = cond_colours, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-7, 7)) +
  labs(title    = "Manipulation check: Δ state valence (post-induction − post-baseline)",
       subtitle = "Positive = valence increased; negative = valence decreased",
       x = NULL, y = "Δ valence") +
  facet_wrap(~participant_id)
```

```{r manip-check-table}
manip_check |>
  select(participant_id, condition,
         manip_check_valence, manip_check_arousal, manip_check_direction_correct) |>
  arrange(participant_id, condition) |>
  kable(digits = 2, caption = "Manipulation check values per participant × condition")
```

### 4.2 Effect of condition on block-end state ratings

```{r anova-valence}
m_valence <- lmer(block_end_valence ~ condition + (1 | participant_id),
                  data = block_end_ratings)
anova(m_valence)
```

```{r posthoc-valence}
emmeans(m_valence, pairwise ~ condition, adjust = "bonferroni")$contrasts |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  arrange(p.value) |>
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "Post-hoc: block_end_valence pairwise comparisons (Bonferroni)")
```

```{r anova-arousal}
m_arousal <- lmer(block_end_arousal ~ condition + (1 | participant_id),
                  data = block_end_ratings)
anova(m_arousal)
```

```{r posthoc-arousal}
emmeans(m_arousal, pairwise ~ condition, adjust = "bonferroni")$contrasts |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  arrange(p.value) |>
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "Post-hoc: block_end_arousal pairwise comparisons (Bonferroni)")
```

### 4.3 Paired comparison plots

```{r paired-plots}
block_end_ratings |>
  pivot_longer(c(block_end_valence, block_end_arousal),
               names_to = "measure", values_to = "value",
               names_prefix = "block_end_") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = condition, y = value, group = participant_id, colour = participant_id)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(1, 7), breaks = 1:7) +
  scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(angle = 30)) +
  facet_wrap(~measure, ncol = 2) +
  labs(title = "Block-end state ratings across conditions",
       x = NULL, y = "Rating (1–7)", colour = "Participant")
```
